title: Imputing Incomplete ISO 8601 Dates with ks_impute_dtc()
text: ISO 8601 dates clinical data sources often truncated: patient visit recorded "2020-03" means “sometime March 2020”, value "2020" means “sometime 2020”. title: Area Under the Curve (AUC) by the trapezoidal rule — ks_auc
text: Linear trapezoid (type = "trapez"): $$AUC_i = \frac{C_i + C_{+1}}{2} \cdot (t_{+1} - t_i)$$ Log-linear trapezoid (type = "log-trapez"): $$AUC_i = \frac{C_{+1} - C_i}{\ln C_{+1} - \ln C_i} \cdot (t_{+1} - t_i)$$ log-linear method preferred elimination phases concentrations decline exponentially.  requires strictly positive concentrations; two consecutive values equal one \(\leq 0\) interval automatically falls back linear rule. Rows sorted c(, time) computing caller need pre-sort data.

Default 0.05. theta0 Null value hypothesis test \(H_0: \theta = \theta_0\). edf Complete-data degrees freedom (positive numeric scalar Inf). Equivalent SAS EDF= option PROC MIANALYZE. finite, Barnard-Rubin (1999) adjusted degrees freedom \(v_m^*\) used instead Rubin (1987) large-sample \(v_m\).  Default Inf (adjustment, Rubin large-sample df). v0 Deprecated alias edf.  Kept backward compatibility; ignored edf also supplied.

text: object class ks_mianalyze components: Estimate Pooled estimate. StdErr Pooled standard error. m Number imputations. Vb -imputation variance. Vw Within-imputation variance. Vt Total variance. df Degrees freedom (adjusted edf finite). r Relative increase variance due nonresponse. lambda Fraction missing information. re Relative efficiency. lcl, ucl Two-sided confidence limits Estimate. alpha Alpha used CI. theta0 Null value used hypothesis test. edf Complete-data degrees freedom used. minim, maxim Min/max input est. t Test statistic \(H_0\). pval Two-sided p-value.

title: Analogue of SAS PROC MIANALYZE (Rubin pooling) — ks_mianalyze
text: Let \(Q_i\) \(U_i\) estimate variance imputation \(\). pooled estimate \(\bar{Q} = m^{-1}\sum_i Q_i\); within variance \(\bar{U} = m^{-1}\sum_i U_i\); variance \(B = (m-1)^{-1}\sum_i (Q_i-\bar{Q})^2\); total variance \(T = \bar{U} + (1 + 1/m)B\). Rubin's (1987) large-sample degrees freedom \(v_m = (m-1)(1 + \bar{U}/((1+m^{-1})B))^2\).  complete-data degrees freedom \(v_0\) small fraction missing information modest, \(v_m\) can greatly exceed \(v_0\), inappropriate.  Barnard-Rubin (1999) adjustment computes \(v_m^* = (1/v_m + 1/\hat{v}_{obs})^{-1}\) \(\hat{v}_{obs} = (1-\gamma) v_0 (v_0+1)/(v_0+3)\) \(\gamma = (1+m^{-1})B/T\).

text: Barnard, J. Rubin, D. B. (1999). Small-sample degrees freedom   multiple imputation. Biometrika, 86, 948–955. Rubin, D. B. (1987). Multiple Imputation Nonresponse Surveys.   Wiley.

title: Newcombe Hybrid Score CI for a difference of two proportions — ks_newcombe_hs
text: Algorithm (Newcombe, 1998): Compute Wilson score CI \([l_i,\, u_i]\) group     level \(1-\alpha\):     $$l_i,\, u_i = \frac{2x_i + z^2 \mp z\sqrt{z^2 + 4x_i(n_i-x_i)/n_i}}{2(n_i + z^2)}$$ Form CI \(\delta = p_1 - p_2\):     $$\mathrm{LCL} = \hat\delta - \sqrt{(p_1-l_1)^2 + (u_2-p_2)^2}$$     $$\mathrm{UCL} = \hat\delta + \sqrt{(u_1-p_1)^2 + (p_2-l_2)^2}$$ function vectorised: vectors length \(k\) supplied, corresponding tuple \((x_{1i}, n_{1i}, x_{2i}, n_{2i})\) processed independently result \(k \times 3\) matrix.

title: Stratified Newcombe Hybrid Score CI for a difference of two proportions — ks_newcombe_hs_strata
text: Algorithm: Compute Wilson CIs \([l_{1i},\,u_{1i}]\)     \([l_{2i},\,u_{2i}]\) stratum \(\). Assign stratum weights     \(W_i = n_{1i}\,n_{2i} / (n_{1i} + n_{2i})\)     (harmonic-mean / Mantel-Haenszel weights). Pooled point estimate:     \(\hat\delta = \sum W_i (p_{1i}-p_{2i}) / \sum W_i\). Pooled lower limit:     $$\mathrm{LCL} = \hat\delta -       \sqrt{\frac{\sum W_i^2(p_{1i}-l_{1i})^2}{(\sum W_i)^2} +             \frac{\sum W_i^2(u_{2i}-p_{2i})^2}{(\sum W_i)^2}}$$ Pooled upper limit: analogously. single stratum reduces un-stratified formula.

title: kstools 0.5.0
text: ks_read_xpt() / ks_write_xpt(): completely rewritten C++ engine.
